title: A Return Address
premise: Aren and Sera turn delivered promises into a witnessed route the city can register. The carrying work earns Aren practical load equipment, an accepted mail delivery and a paid round; a local beacon contradicts its maintenance record.

panels.current_state: Continues N1-48 without reset. Aren owns brass rectangular Lower Post badge on red cord, earned pay, closed cream wallet at belt and outgoing bundle including petition. Sword sheathed anatomical RIGHT hip; no line. Existing LEFT-elbow sleeve tear and lower-hem tear persist; shoulder still sore.

panels.current_state: Hold brakes the moving holder and his carried load by sustained concentration; no added force or range. One taut pommel-to-post line during final braking instant, then supported feet. No strike or speech while concentrating. No new tear/injury.

He places the gray bag on the table and opens it, allowing the attendant to lift the ordinary outgoing letters into separate sorting trays. The folded old single strap remains tied to the bag side.

copy.text: All seals dry.

Aren takes the receipt with his left hand, leaving the accepted mail behind in the occupied sorting trays. Sera watches from the accessible staff doorway at the table’s side after taking the ordinary perimeter walkway.

copy.text: Thank you for writing the return address in full.

copy.speaker: Ossa
copy.text: They have written us a return address. In their own book.

panels.action: Ossa places the agreed inspection payment in Aren’s hand and pins a plain morning collection schedule beside the open entrance. Aren looks from his assigned round to the quiet chair at the sorting table and finally sits down for a moment.

copy.speaker: Ossa
copy.text: The morning round is paid work, if you want it.

copy.speaker: Aren
copy.text: I want it.

panels.camera: medium seated relief with posted schedule as secondary object

panels.action: From the chair Aren notices a small empty room above the sorting hall through its open stair door: plain walls, one square window, enough space for a bed. Ossa follows his glance and rests a hand on the banister. His face holds anticipation rather than triumph over a new enemy.

copy.speaker: Ossa
copy.text: Ask me about the rent after your first week.

copy.speaker: Aren
copy.text: I will.

panels.current_state: Aren has not acquired the room or a key yet; he still owns earned wages and recurring work. This is a concrete future choice, not cancelled reward. No magic, no new gear or costume change.

panels.action: Pell lays an old maintenance copy beside Sera’s new signed survey work order on the sorting table. He points through the open stair window to a small cyan route beacon on the nearby lift structure. Its steady light is plainly visible in daylight; no creature is shown beside it.

copy.speaker: Pell
copy.text: That beacon was marked dark when they closed the circuit.

copy.speaker: Sera
copy.text: Then we start by finding its supply.

panels.camera: medium work-order-to-real-beacon sightline
panels.current_state: Sera has authorized a local safety survey after route inspection; this is NOT the Office’s pending petition reply. Pell owns old maintenance copy. Present clue only: local beacon glows although older record marked it dark. No cause, sabotage culprit or later repair revealed.

panels.action: Outside, the repaired postal entrance stays open below the small steadily lit beacon on its neighboring lift tower. In a warm foreground window, Aren, Ossa, Pell and Sera bend over the real work orders around their table. The city beyond is vast and inhabited; their one registered route is a modest bright part of it.

copy.speaker: Aren
copy.text: After the morning post. They know where to send the answer now.
